summary: chain-analyze bundles decrypt-then-exec loader pulling payload from unpinned `chain-manager` dep
details: The package publishes as `chain-analyze` under an author string impersonating Theta Labs and advertises a Theta blockchain SDK, but `package.json`'s declared `main` (`dist/chain-analyze.cjs.js`) is absent from the tarball. The shipped bundles under a mismatched name — `dist/sigchain-js.cjs.js`, `dist/sigchain-js.esm.js`, `dist/sigchain-js.umd.js` — contain top-level code that imports `desKey` (and a variant `rsaToken` via `readRSAFromPackage()`) from the unpinned dependency `chain-manager` pinned to `latest`, DES-decrypts the ciphertext with a hardcoded `PASSWORD`, spawns a child `node` process, and pipes the decrypted string to its stdin. This is a load-time arbitrary-code loader whose payload the publisher rotates by pushing new versions of the sibling `chain-manager` package; every `require`/`import` of these bundles executes attacker-controlled JavaScript on the installer's host. Wallet, private-key, and signing code paths advertised by the SDK sit alongside the loader, so consumers building against the Theta-branded API surface trigger the RCE primitive on module load.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
